title: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)

sections.label: Housing supply increase
sections.summary: 9,250 private housing units were released in 2023 and HDB targets 19,600 BTO flats in 2024, with the property market appearing to abate.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: With a record 9,250 private housing units released in 2023, the highest in a decade, and the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) 2024 target to complete 19,600 Build-To-Order (BTO) flats amongst other initiatives, housing supply has increased significantly, with signs of a property market appearing to abate.

sections.label: Interim housing for divorcees
sections.summary: MND is asked whether it will consider interim housing for divorcees with special needs children still finalising their divorce, or a PPHS Open Market voucher-like scheme.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Will MND consider providing interim housing for divorcees with special needs children and are still in the process of finalising their divorce, or provide a scheme that is quite similar to that of a PPHS Open Market voucher?

sections.label: Community Care Apartments popularity
sections.summary: Community Care Apartments in Bukit Batok integrate residential units with a hawker centre, activity centre and community gardens, and have proven popular for enabling ageing well.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: More recently, the Community Care Apartments in Bukit Batok, whereby residential units will be integrated with a hawker centre, activity centre and community gardens, have proven to be popular for its refreshed idea in enabling ageing well, while not institutionalising residential living in a nursing home.

sections.label: Housing access for mixed-status couples
sections.summary: Access to BTO or SBF, grants and housing loan assessment is impacted if a spouse is not already a PR, and additional rules are suggested to support this group.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Today, their access to BTO or Sale of Balance Flats (SBF), grants and housing loan assessment, are impacted if their spouse is not already a Permanent Resident (PR).

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could we not consider some form of additional rules to be added to existing ones so that we can also enable support to this group of Singaporeans?

sections.label: Delayed BTO projects
sections.summary: 28% of BTO projects delayed by the pandemic remain under construction, and around 22,000 affected households will progressively receive keys by the first quarter of 2025 or earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, 28% of the BTO projects delayed by the pandemic remain under construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For these projects, around 22,000 affected households will progressively receive their keys by the first quarter of 2025 or earlier.

sections.label: HDB improvement project delays
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how many HDB improvement projects, including those done by Town Councils, were affected by contractor difficulties and how many remain uncompleted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how many of such HDB improvement projects, including those undertaken on HDB's behalf by Town Councils, have been affected by contractors facing difficulties, as manifested by the number of extensions requested, and how many remain uncompleted?

sections.label: HDB Plus project subsidies
sections.summary: DPM Lawrence Wong said HDB will roll out its first Plus project later this year, and MND was asked for subsidy and pricing details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has shared that HDB will roll out its first Plus project later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MND share more details and examples of the likely level of subsidies, as well as the broad pricing trends of Plus and Prime housing in the coming two to three years so as to ensure that both of these categories of flats will remain within the reach of Singaporeans from different income groups?

sections.label: PSP rental vouchers and apartments
sections.summary: PSP welcomes one-year PPHS rental vouchers for couples awaiting BTO flats and urges the Government to consider its Millennial Apartments Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) welcomes the Government's move to support the urgent housing needs of couples who are waiting for their BTO flats to be completed, with one-year rental vouchers under PPHS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are happy to see that the Government has further recognised that rental apartments play an important role in meeting the housing needs of our younger Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the PPHS voucher scheme is temporary and may drive up rents for some groups of Singaporean tenants, such as single mothers, LGBTs and couples who do not qualify under PPHS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to go further and consider PSP's Millennial Apartments Scheme as a new policy to develop rental apartments into a viable, alternative housing for younger Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singles flat age and co-living
sections.summary: The speaker says the eligible age of 35 for singles to own HDB flats is appropriate and calls for co-living facilities in the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, I have said before that the current eligible age of 35 years old for singles to own HDB flats is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: That said, I have also called on the Government to consider co‐living facilities in the heartlands to allow young singles to live, work and play together before they move on to different phase in life, essentially short-term, flexible rental for young singles.

sections.label: No plans for rental subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker says there are no plans to provide such rental subsidies and agrees with MND's varied rental options and subsidies for couples renting from the open market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As such, we have no plans to provide such rental subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am gratified that MND and HDB have finally changed its policies in response to feedback, even if it includes one brought up by an Opposition Member of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I agree with the MND's plans to provide more varied rental options, such as piloting new service apartments and shared facility public rental housing and more importantly, provide subsidies for couples needing help in renting from the open market.

sections.label: S-Pass holders in rented flats
sections.summary: Seventy percent of S-Pass holders reside in rented HDB flats, and the Minister is asked whether rental programmes will be updated and expanded beyond pilots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Seventy-percent of S-Pass holders currently reside in rented HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To that end, I would like to ask the Minister the following: The Forward Singapore exercise has emphasised that there will be an affordable home for every budget and need; and that the public housing programmes need to be updated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In that regard, can the Minister share whether the rental programmes are also in line for updating and expansion beyond these pilots?

sections.label: PRS households space constraints
sections.summary: The roughly 50,000 households under the PRS today do not have a restful home because of space constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The roughly 50,000 households under the PRS today, do not have this luxury of a restful home because of space constraints.

sections.label: Co-living rental housing for singles
sections.summary: Recommends MND offer more co-living rental housing for singles, de-stigmatise public rental housing, and tier rent subsidies with one to five year leases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We need to make affordable and pleasant housing options accessible for people in all life stages and circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I recommend MND to offer more co-living rental housing options for singles at all ages, and de-stigmatise public rental housing from the current image that is, "only for the poor".

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The rent subsidies can be tiered according to each tenant's household and income situation, with lease terms ranging from one to five years, with transition out to home ownership as the eventual goal.

sections.label: Joint Single Scheme Operator-Run launch
sections.summary: The Joint Single Scheme (JSS) Operator-Run was launched in December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, on the Joint Single Scheme (JSS) Operator-Run, which was launched in December 2021.

sections.label: 3-room PRS units created
sections.summary: Asks how many 3-room PRS units have been created to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, how many 3-room PRS units have been created to date?

sections.label: SERS projects identified since 1995
sections.summary: Since August 1995, HDB has identified 78 SERS projects, with four more in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since August 1995, HDB has identified a total of 78 SERS projects with an additional four in the pipeline.

sections.label: Terms less generous than SERS
sections.summary: HDB stated the terms will be less generous than those under SERS, and people have been told to stay tuned since 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We have been told to stay tuned, since 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But HDB stated that the terms will be less generous than those offered under SERS.

sections.label: PPHS supply and rental voucher
sections.summary: HDB committed to doubling PPHS flat supply by 2025 and announced a rental voucher for the open market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: HDB has committed to doubling its supply of flats under PPHS by 2025 and also announced a rental voucher to be used in the open market.

sections.label: Falling total fertility rate
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate fell to 0.97 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our TFR has fallen to 0.97 in 2023.

sections.label: HDB building Shorter Waiting Time flats
sections.summary: HDB builds about 20,000 units yearly on average, of which only 2,000 to 3,000 are Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: HDB is currently building about 20,000 units per year on average, but only 2,000 to 3,000 are Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sections.label: Political will and single unwed parents
sections.summary: Major changes need political will, and single unwed parents can now get a public rental flat or buy a BTO flat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The political will to implement major changes is needed if we really want to turn it around.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that single unwed parents are now allowed to get a public rental flat or buy a BTO flat.

sections.label: Single unwed parents and PPHS
sections.summary: Single unwed parents should be treated the same as others for PPHS, and Lawrence Wong announced one-year PPHS vouchers for eligible families to rent HDB flats in the open market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Single unwed parents should be treated the same as others when applying for PPHS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I welcome Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s announcement that the Government will provide one-year PPHS voucher for eligible families to rent HDB flats in the open market.

sections.label: Lift Upgrading Programme gazetted
sections.summary: HDB recently gazetted the Lift Upgrading Programme for 10 HDB flat units at Block 833 Hougang Central.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: HDB recently gazetted the Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP) for 10 units of HDB flats at Block 833 Hougang Central.

sections.label: HDB blocks without direct lift access
sections.summary: Desmond Lee said that as of January 2023 about 140 HDB blocks had units without direct lift access on the same floor, due to technical and site constraints or high costs, some exceeding $100,000 per unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee replied to me at last year's Committee of Supply (COS) that as of January 2023, there were about 140 HDB blocks with units without direct access to lifts on the same floor and that they are due to technical and site constraints or high costs, some of which exceeded $100,000 per unit.

sections.label: Aljunied-Hougang excluded from LUP committee
sections.summary: Aljunied-Hougang Town Council was not included in the Working Committee during the LUP's design and implementation stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, Aljunied-Hougang Town Council was not included in the Working Committee during the design and implementation stage for the LUP.

sections.label: Prioritising older flats for HIP
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to HDB to prioritise older flats for the Home Improvement Programme given their age and condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Considering the age and conditions of these flats, may I appeal to HDB to prioritise older flats for Home Improvement Programme (HIP) too so that a more comprehensive upgrading works can be done for these flats?

sections.label: Proposals on lift funding and funds
sections.summary: The speaker proposes rebalancing Sinking Fund and LRF proportions, broadening LRF use for lift components, and allowing transfers between the funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, expensive lift components like their automatic rescue device, the main controller PCB, the emergency battery-operated power supply and the uninterrupted power supply can only utilise the Routine Fund, despite their considerable capital expense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to put forth three proposals to MND: first, rebalance the funding distribution between the Sinking Fund and the LRF, slightly increasing the Sinking Fund's proportion and reducing the LRF's proportion; second, broaden the permissible applications of the LRF to encompass all lift components with a lifespan exceeding 10 years; and third, permit Town Councils to transfer funds between the LRF and Sinking Fund to fund necessary cyclical works without compromising the original intent of setting aside adequate reserves for the two funds.

sections.label: More lifts for 140 blocks
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to allocate more resources to install additional lifts at 140 blocks, starting with Nanyang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given Singapore's ageing society, I urge the Minister to allocate more resources to install additional lifts at the mentioned 140 blocks, starting with Nanyang perhaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The rapid increase in general construction costs, which rose about 30%-40% from 2021 to 2023, with anticipated further appreciation in 2024.

sections.label: One-time fund top-up for projects
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MND will provide a one-time fund top-up for approved projects in the last two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Specifically, whether MND is prepared to provide a one-time fund top-up for approved projects in the last two years to address the impact of escalating construction costs.

sections.label: Coffee shop bidding and food prices
sections.summary: The speaker shared data on Sengkang coffee shop food prices and suggested changing the bidding away from the price quality method.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: During last year's Committee of Supply, I shared data that volunteers and I had collected, showing that the difference between coffee shop food in Sengkang versus mature estates amounts to around 50 cents, which is significant for many families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I had suggested then, that the bidding for coffee shop spaces could be altered away from the current price quality method (PQM), to a system where the winning bidder would be awarded the price of the second-highest bid.

sections.label: Budget meals and coffee shop rentals
sections.summary: It states a substantial weighting in the PQM for factors like promised budget meals would not be needed, and that almost all HDB-owned coffee shops did not raise rentals over five years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: It would not need to introduce a substantial weighting in the PQM that includes factors, such as whether budget meals are promised by bidders.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: It was recently revealed to this House that among half of coffee shops owned by HDB, almost all of them did not choose to increase their rentals over the past five years.

sections.label: Budget meal requirement in PQM
sections.summary: MND works the budget meal requirement into the PQM matrix and publicises where cheap meals are sold, but the framework requires only one budget meal, yielding few plain options.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The current strategy is for MND to content itself with working with the budget meal requirement into the PQM matrix and to publicise where one may purchase such cheap meals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But since the framework only requires that vendors offer at least one budget meal, in reality, this translates into each coffee shop offering only a small handful of very plain vanilla options, think fishball noodles or two-vegetables one-meat cai fan or kopi and teh-o.

sections.label: Budget meal condition for Outdoor Refreshment Areas
sections.summary: In July 2023, the speaker suggested HDB impose the budget meal and drink requirement on privately-owned coffee shops as a condition for renewing permission to use Outdoor Refreshment Areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In July 2023, I suggested that HDB impose the budget meal and drink requirement on such privately-owned coffee shops as a condition for the renewal of permission to use Outdoor Refreshment Areas.

sections.label: Draft Master Plan 2025 design
sections.summary: Leveraging on these engagements, the URA is designing the Draft Master Plan 2025, which details land use for the next 10 to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Leveraging on these engagements, the URA is designing the Draft Master Plan 2025 that details land use for next 10 to 15 years.

sections.label: Approach to land allocation review
sections.summary: It asks what approach the Ministry is adopting to rethink land allocation, classification of use and preservation of heritage assets in the Draft Master Plan review, given competing land use needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: With more competing needs for land use, what approach is the Ministry adopting to rethink about land allocation, classification of use and preservation of heritage assets in the Draft Master Plan review?

sections.label: Vertical zoning and mixed-use developments
sections.summary: It states that blurring lines of work and leisure entail new options for defining land demarcation, and that vertical zoning of used spaces and more mixed-use developments may become more pronounced.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Blurring lines of work and leisure entails new options of how we define new land demarcation. "Vertical zoning" of used spaces and increased number of mixed-use developments may become more pronounced.

sections.label: Citizen involvement in land use
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government intends to involve citizens and residents in planning future land use under the Forward SG movement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: As part of the Forward SG movement, may I ask the Minister, how is the Government intending to involve citizens and residents in Singapore as we plan for future land use?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, over the years, this House has raised questions about the urban heat island effect, with studies showing a difference of 7 degrees celsius between urban and less built-up areas of Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore population density
sections.summary: The overall population density of Singapore is around 8,000 persons per square kilometre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The overall population density of Singapore is around 8,000 persons per square kilometres.

sections.label: Freelance delivery riders and drivers
sections.summary: The passage describes over 20,000 freelance riders and drivers on foot, two-wheels or four-wheels who deliver convenience and everyday comforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, they are the 20,000-over freelance riders and drivers on foot, two-wheels or four-wheels, who deliver convenience and everyday comforts to us.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup for Last-mile Delivery
sections.summary: NDCA is involved in a Tripartite Workgroup for Last-mile Delivery led by URA and LTA with other delivery ecosystem stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NDCA is involved in a Tripartite Workgroup for Last-mile Delivery led by Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) and Land Transport Authority (LTA) and comprising other delivery ecosystem stakeholders.

sections.label: Incentives for delivery-friendly properties
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry would consider incentives for mature properties that become delivery-friendly.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, with deliveries becoming a mainstay, would the Ministry consider introducing incentives for mature properties that become delivery-friendly?

sections.label: Draft Master Plan 2025 engagement
sections.summary: MND is working on detailed land use plans for the next 10 to 15 years in DMP 2025 and conducting a public engagement exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Based on the collected feedback from that exercise, MND is now working on the detailed land use plans for the next 10 to 15 years in the Draft Master Plan (DMP) 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For DMP 2025, the Ministry is also conducting a public engagement exercise to gain a better understanding of the needs and aspirations of our people for their estates and our nation.

sections.label: Bishan estate amenities and flats
sections.summary: Bishan has no wet market or hawker centre, a polyclinic is planned by 2030, and 2,000 more HDB flats will be added in two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Bishan estate currently has no wet market or a hawker centre while a polyclinic is planned to be up by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the next two to three years, another 2,000 HDB flats will be added.

sections.label: VERS criteria and EASE accessibility
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on VERS criteria and implementation, notes HDB allows PwDs to qualify for EASE without meeting age criteria, and asks MND to add improvement items like induction stoves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Minister provide an update on the progress of the Ministry's deliberations over the details for the criteria and implementation of the VERS Scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, HDB actually allows PwDs to qualify for Enhancement for Active Citizens (EASE) even if they do not meet the age criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, could MND increase the list of improvement items under EASE, beyond things like slip-resistant floor tiles, grab bars and ramps, to cover more accessibility needs like induction stoves for the safety of the visually impaired?

sections.label: Proximity housing grants for PwDs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MND could consider enhanced proximity housing grants for PwDs buying a flat near parents or siblings who provide caregiving support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, could MND consider implementing enhanced proximity housing grants for PwDs purchasing a flat near their parents or siblings, who provide essential caregiving support?

sections.label: EASE 2.0 rollout and criteria
sections.summary: The passage asks when HDB will start rolling out EASE 2.0, what criteria will select precincts, and when most eligible precincts will be covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: First of all, with regard to EASE, when will HDB start rolling out the EASE 2.0 programme and what criteria will be used to select the precincts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: And when does HDB expect to cover most eligible precincts for EASE 2.0?

sections.label: Incentives for clinic operating hours
sections.summary: The passage asks whether HDB could provide rental subsidies or try shared clinic spaces or night relief GPs until extended operating hours can be a tender requirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, HDB perhaps cannot mandate them to extend their operating hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But could HDB provide incentives in the form of rental subsidies or experiment with formats, like shared clinic spaces or night relief GPs, until it can be made a tender requirement at the next renewal?

sections.label: Centralised planning for HDB services
sections.summary: The passage states oversaturation of some services leaves residents lacking other options and urges centralised planning to prioritise essential services like clinics, pharmacies, eldercare and childcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: This can result in an oversaturation of certain types of services, leaving residents lacking access to other essential or desired options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: I urge the Government to adopt a more centralised planning approach to ensure a diversity of services within HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Essential services, like clinics, pharmacies, eldercare and childcare facilities, should be prioritised.

sections.label: Variation Order approval and disbursement
sections.summary: MND is asked to work with LTA and PUB on policy adjustments for prompt approval and partial disbursement of Variation Orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: In particular, would MND work with key Government agencies, specifically the Land Transport Authority (LTA), Public Utilities Board (PUB), to consider policy adjustments, such as changing the framework to ensure prompt approval and to allow for partial disbursement of Variation Orders (VOs), especially for the big and prolonged projects that usually have high-value VOs?

sections.label: Scoring system for local construction companies
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it would review the scoring system to include points for local construction companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider a review of the scoring system to include points for local construction companies?

sections.label: Built environment ITM digitalisation refresh
sections.summary: In 2022 the built environment ITM was refreshed to improve the value-chain approach through digitalisation, including Integrated Digital Delivery.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In 2022, the built environment ITM was refreshed with a focus on improving the value-chain approach through digitalisation; with the incorporation of the Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD) in projects in the Built Environment sector as a case in point.

sections.label: Industry transformation progress update
sections.summary: The Government is asked for an update on the progress of the industry transformation after two years of implementation.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Can the Government provide an update on the progress of the industry transformation after two years of its implementation?

sections.label: Low-carbon Built Environment transition
sections.summary: With buildings accounting for over 20% of carbon emissions, the question asks what efforts have been taken to accelerate the low-carbon transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: With buildings accounting for over 20% of our carbon emissions, what efforts have we taken to accelerate our transition to a low-carbon Built Environment?

sections.label: COP15 blue spaces commitment
sections.summary: At COP15, a commitment was made to conserve 30% of blue spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At COP15, we committed to conserving 30% of our blue spaces.

sections.label: More Marine Parks
sections.summary: The Government is asked whether it will consider designating more marine sites as Marine Parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider designating more marine sites as Marine Parks?

sections.label: City in Nature Progress
sections.summary: An update is sought on progress four years after MND announced its vision to transform Singapore into a city in nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: It would be hard to have trees without nests in them and correspondingly hear the uwu calls, or healthy longgangs without fishes and otters, or beautiful flowers without bees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: It has been four years since MND announced its vision to transform Singapore into a city in nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Can we have an update on the progress?

sections.label: Sisters Island Marine Park
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about Sisters Island enhancement completion, park opening, public access to Big Sisters Island, visitor caps, and a second marine park.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Enhancement works to Sisters Island are slated to complete this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update on when the park will be opened, how the public can access Big Sisters Island, and any visitor caps that will be imposed to manage the carrying capacity?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: Is the Government considering a second marine park in Singapore?

sections.label: COVID-19 and Rock Pigeons
sections.summary: NParks' 2021 survey found that reduced food sources due to COVID-19 lowered rock pigeon numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: NParks’ own survey in 2021 found that the reduction in food sources due to COVID-19 reduced the numbers of rock pigeons.

sections.label: High-Rise Littering Presumption
sections.summary: A presumption clause presumes flat owners or tenants committed littering from a flat unless they prove otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: To tackle high-rise littering which similarly relies on enforcement through surveillance, we introduced a presumption clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Where it is proved that littering acts have been committed from a flat, the owners or tenants will be presumed to have committed the offence unless they prove otherwise.

sections.label: Animal Abuse Cases Surge
sections.summary: In 2023, Singapore saw a 79% surge in animal abuse cases under investigation, the highest in 11 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In 2023, Singapore witnessed a staggering 79% surge in cases of animal abuse under investigation, the highest number in 11 years.

sections.label: Animal abuse punishment
sections.summary: First-time animal abuse offenders face a maximum fine of up to $15,000 and/or 18 months' jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The current punishment for animal abuse is a maximum fine of up to $15,000 and/or an 18 months jail term for first-time offenders.

sections.label: Municipal Services Office tenth year
sections.summary: 2024 marks the 10th year since the Municipal Services Office was set up.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Chairman, 2024 marks the 10th year since the Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up.

sections.label: Love Our Hood initiative update
sections.summary: The 2021 Love Our Hood initiative with Mountbatten, Pioneer and Bukit Gombak seeks community-based solutions, and an update is requested.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Back in 2021, it also saw the introduction of the Love Our Hood initiative in partnership with Mountbatten, Pioneer and Bukit Gombak Constituency Offices that seeks to provide residents and community stakeholders to co-develop community-based solutions to manage municipal issues and foster neighbourliness.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister provide an update on the progress of this initiative and any intention to further scale up the initiative for effective resolution of community issues?

sections.label: Love Our Hood learnings
sections.summary: The passage asks whether learnings from Love Our Hood can be leveraged for noise, second-hand smoking and pigeon feeding.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Can we leverage the learnings from the Love Our Hood initiative?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: These include noise between units, second-hand smoking and the pigeon feeding.

sections.label: Co-creating community solutions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether users or affected persons should co-create community solutions rather than only being urged to show consideration.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Beyond imploring for residents to just exercise more consideration, should we not take the opportunity to have users or those possibly affected to co-create community solutions to address these municipal issues?

sections.label: Supporting homeownership aspirations
sections.summary: Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will speak on low-income households and seniors, and the commitment to remain a nation of homeowners is stated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And my colleague, Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim will speak on what we are doing for low-income households and our seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are firmly committed to supporting Singaporeans' aspirations to own their homes and determined that we shall remain a nation of homeowners.

sections.label: 100,000 new flats commitment
sections.summary: The government committed in 2021 to launching 100,000 new flats by 2025, with over 67,000 launched as of February this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: To address this imbalance, we committed in 2021 to launching 100,000 new flats by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As of February this year, we have launched more than 67,000 flats, or two-thirds of our commitment.

sections.label: Chencharu housing and Khatib MRT
sections.summary: Chencharu will be served by Khatib MRT, with a first BTO project of around 1,200 flats launching in June and plans for around 10,000 homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Future residents in Chencharu will be served by Khatib MRT and other connectivity initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will launch the first BTO project of around 1,200 flats in June this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Over time, we plan to build around 10,000 homes in Chencharu, at least 80% of which will be public housing.

sections.label: Former barracks redevelopment studies
sections.summary: Former barracks tenancies expire by 2030, and environmental and heritage studies for possible public and private housing redevelopment start in the second quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Many of the former barracks are currently tenanted out for interim uses, with tenancies expiring progressively by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are studying the possibility of redeveloping the site for a mix of public and private housing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Residents will also have easy access to green and recreational spaces such as the Southern Ridges and Labrador Nature Park Network.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will start environmental and heritage studies in the second quarter of this year.

sections.label: Standard, Plus and Prime flats
sections.summary: A new national housing framework of Standard, Plus and Prime flats takes effect later this year to maintain social mix and fair subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We also want our estates to maintain a good social mix and that the distribution of subsidies to be fair.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have therefore introduced the new national housing framework of Standard, Plus and Prime flats, which will take effect later this year.

sections.label: Grants for resale flat buyers
sections.summary: Eligible First-Timer families can receive up to $190,000 in grants with the EHG and Proximity Housing Grant when buying a resale flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Together with the EHG, as well as the Proximity Housing Grant, eligible First-Timer families can receive up to $190,000 in grants when they purchase a resale flat.

sections.label: Deferred income assessment for couples
sections.summary: Since 2018, more than 3,700 couples have used deferred income assessment with SDS support to ease upfront costs and start home ownership early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, since 2018, more than 3,700 couples have tapped on the deferred income assessment, with support from the SDS, to ease their upfront costs and start their home ownership journey early.

sections.label: Staggered Downpayment Scheme enhancement
sections.summary: The Staggered Downpayment Scheme will be enhanced by reducing initial downpayment to 2.5% of flat price for couples using deferred income assessment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To provide further support to these young couples who tap on the deferred income assessment, we will enhance the Staggered Downpayment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will do this by reducing their initial downpayment to 2.5% of their flat price.

sections.label: Balance downpayment at key collection
sections.summary: These couples will pay the balance downpayment at key collection, effective from the next sales launch in June this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These couples will pay the balance downpayment at key collection, when they are in a better position to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This will take effect from the next sales launch in June this year.

sections.label: Shorter Waiting Time flats launch
sections.summary: About 2,800 Shorter Waiting Time flats will be launched in 2024, one year ahead of the 2025 target of 2,000 to 3,000 flats yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In February last year, we had shared that we would launch 2000 to 3,000 of such flats per year by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But because of the hard work of my colleagues at HDB, we are now able to do this one year ahead of our target, to launch about 2,800 Shorter Waiting Time flats in 2024.

sections.label: Singles buying 2-room Flexi BTO flats
sections.summary: Singles will be allowed to purchase 2-room Flexi BTO flats islandwide, Prime, Plus and Standard, from the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I have mentioned earlier, we will be allowing singles to purchase 2-room Flexi BTO flats islandwide, Prime, Plus and Standard, from the second half of this year.

sections.label: PPHS flat supply increase
sections.summary: Since 2021, the supply of PPHS flats has more than doubled to 2,000 units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since 2021, we have more than doubled our supply of PPHS flats to 2,000 units.

sections.label: Application rates and supply ramp up
sections.summary: Application rates dropped from over 20 times in 2021 to 2.3 times in February this year, with supply ramping up to 4,000 units by next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Application rates have dropped from over 20 times in 2021 in the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, to 2.3 times in February this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In recent exercises, all married applicants with children, including expectant parents, were invited to select a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will press on with our supply ramp up to 4,000 units by next year.

sections.label: Rental support for eligible families
sections.summary: Each eligible family will receive $300 per month whether they rent an HDB flat or an HDB bedroom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Each eligible family will receive $300 per month, regardless of whether they rent an HDB flat or an HDB bedroom.

sections.label: PPHS Voucher one-year period
sections.summary: The PPHS Voucher will run for a year from July 2024, and its impact on the rental market will be monitored closely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The PPHS Voucher will be in place for a year starting from July 2024, and we will monitor the impact of the voucher on the rental market closely.

sections.label: Age Well SG spending
sections.summary: $600 million will be spent on Age Well SG initiatives to help seniors age actively and independently in their communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To do so, we will spend $600 million on Age Well SG initiatives, to help our seniors age actively and independently in their communities.

sections.label: IDD adoption rate increase
sections.summary: IDD adoption for new developments by GFA rose from about 45% in 2022 to 58% in 2023, on track for 70% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The IDD adoption rate for new developments by gross floor area (GFA) has increased from about 45% in 2022, to 58% in 2023 and we are on track to meeting our target of 70% IDD adoption by 2025.

sections.label: DfMA adoption rate increase
sections.summary: DfMA adoption for all new developments by GFA increased from 51% in 2022 to 61% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The DfMA adoption rate for all new developments by GFA increased from 51% in 2022 to 61% in 2023.

sections.label: CRS registration for construction firms
sections.summary: All firms hiring foreign construction workers must register under the CRS, which becomes the sole gateway for these workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This should apply equally to firms, regardless of whether they undertake public or private sector projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will now require all firms hiring foreign construction workers to be registered under the CRS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: CRS will become the sole gateway for firms to access these workers.

sections.label: CRS entry requirements adjusted
sections.summary: CRS entry requirements will be adjusted to require minimum paid-up capital of $50,000 and a $300,000 three-year track record, with time given to meet them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, for a start, the CRS entry requirements will be adjusted to keep pace with current tender prices and construction costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, to be registered, we will require a firm to have a minimum paid-up capital of $50,000 and a track record of $300,000 in total over the past three years, or about $100,000 per year on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is to ensure that firms that hire foreign construction workers have the minimum financial capability and experience to sustain their operations and deliver projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will give our firms time to meet these new requirements.

sections.label: Downpayment cut and rental voucher
sections.summary: Initial downpayment will be reduced to 2.5% of flat price, and from July a one-year $300 monthly voucher will help families renting while awaiting BTO completion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To further alleviate their burden, we will reduce the initial downpayment to 2.5% of the flat price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Starting from July this year, the Government will implement a one-year voucher to assist families who are waiting for their BTO flat to be completed and have to rent a flat in the open market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Eligible families can receive a monthly voucher of $300 to defray their rental expenses.

sections.label: Long-Term Plan Review engagement
sections.summary: From 2021 to 2022, over 15,000 Singaporeans were engaged on the Long-Term Plan Review to map strategies for Singapore's development.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: From 2021 to 2022, we engaged over 15,000 Singaporeans on the Long-Term Plan Review to map out strategies to guide Singapore's development for the next 50 years and beyond.

sections.label: Draft Master Plan 2025 engagement
sections.summary: As announced by Minister Desmond Lee in October 2023, Singaporeans will be engaged on the Draft Master Plan 2025, which has four broad themes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As announced by Minister Desmond Lee in October 2023 last year, we will be engaging a wide range of Singaporeans on the Draft Master Plan 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The four broad themes for the Draft Master Plan are: shaping a happy, healthy city; strengthening urban resilience; enabling sustainable growth; and stewarding nature and heritage.

sections.label: Long Island reclamation project
sections.summary: The "Long Island" project plans to reclaim about 800 hectares of land off East Coast to meet multiple needs for existing and future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: An example is the "Long Island" project, our plan to reclaim about 800 hectares of land off East Coast. "Long Island" will be an opportunity to meet multiple needs for our existing and future generations.

sections.label: Engagement activities and exhibition
sections.summary: Engagements will include roadshows, focus group discussions, collaborations with professional bodies and competitions, culminating in the Draft Master Plan 2025 exhibition in the second half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our engagements will encompass roadshows, focus group discussions, collaborations with professional bodies and competitions where people can submit their ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These engagements will culminate in the Draft Master Plan 2025 exhibition which will be held in the second half of 2025 at the URA Centre and selected locations around the island.

sections.label: Greening buildings energy standards
sections.summary: Minimum energy performance standards were raised and a Green Mark incentive scheme launched, with a Mandatory Energy Improvement regime coming by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2021 and 2022, we raised minimum energy performance standards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This is so that new buildings are designed to be sustainable and existing buildings upgraded to meet higher sustainability standards.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also launched the S$63 million Green Mark Incentive Scheme for Existing Buildings 2.0 in 2022, which provides support to building owners for energy efficiency retrofits.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These efforts have enabled us to green about 58% of our buildings by GFA to date.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: To help meet our target of greening 80% of our buildings by 2030, we will be introducing the Mandatory Energy Improvement, or MEI, regime by the end of this year, as announced by Senior Minister of State Tan last year.

sections.label: Base Tier construction equipment funding
sections.summary: Eligible local construction firms can receive up to 70% funding support for pre-approved energy-efficient construction equipment, capped at S$30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the Base Tier, eligible local construction firms can receive up to 70% of funding support for pre-approved energy-efficient construction equipment, with a cap of S$30,000.

sections.label: Data analysis improving project processes
sections.summary: Collected data can be analysed to improve processes for future projects, expected to raise productivity by up to 50% and reduce downstream abortive works.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The data collected can also be analysed to improve processes for future projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This initiative is expected to increase productivity by up to 50% over existing project workflows and reduce downstream abortive works.

sections.label: Capability Transfer Programme support
sections.summary: WSG's Capability Transfer Programme facilitates transfer of capabilities from foreign specialists to locals, with salary support, attachment costs and equipment and venue funding.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For instance, Workforce Singapore's (WSG's) Capability Transfer Programme facilitates the transfer of capabilities from foreign specialists to locals.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Companies can benefit from salary support, attachment-related costs and funding for equipment and venue costs for industry-wide projects.

sections.label: SME public sector construction contracts
sections.summary: Over 80% of public sector construction contracts were awarded to SMEs last year, and the Government will review procurement processes for fairness and cost-effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Last year, more than 80% of public sector construction contracts were awarded to small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to conduct regular reviews to ensure that our procurement processes remain fair and cost-effective.

sections.label: Neighbourhood Renewal Programme extension
sections.summary: The fifth phase of the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme is extended to HDB blocks built up to 1999, benefiting more than 100,000 additional flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: A key component involves extending the upcoming fifth phase of the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme, or NRP, to HDB blocks built up to 1999.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This will benefit more than 100,000 additional flats, as previously, only blocks built up to 1995 were eligible.

sections.label: Fifth phase NRP precinct selection
sections.summary: The first batch of precincts to be upgraded under the fifth phase of NRP will be selected by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The first batch of precincts to be upgraded under the fifth phase of NRP will be selected by the end of this year.

sections.label: Spalling concrete repair assistance scheme
sections.summary: If residents report spalling concrete within the flat, HDB will tell the flat owner about the Goodwill Repair Assistance Scheme, which subsidises 50% of repair costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As for spalling concrete within the flat, if reported by residents, HDB will let the flat owner know about the Goodwill Repair Assistance Scheme, under which HDB will subsidise 50% of the repair costs.

sections.label: Lift Access Housing Grant
sections.summary: A Lift Access Housing Grant of up to $30,000 helps homeowners who urgently need direct lift access or live in blocks that cannot undergo LUP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In some of these cases, the cost can be more than $200,000 per benefiting household.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Therefore, we have measures for households that urgently need direct lift access or those who live in blocks that cannot undergo LUP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We offer a Lift Access Housing Grant of up to $30,000 to help these homeowners buy a flat with direct lift access.

sections.label: Lift Replacement Fund introduction
sections.summary: The LRF was introduced in 2017 because Town Councils had been significantly under-saving for lift replacements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In particular, the LRF was introduced in 2017 because Town Councils had been significantly under-saving for lift replacements.

sections.label: Budget meals at HDB coffee shops
sections.summary: By 2026, all 374 coffee shops rented from HDB will offer budget meals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: By 2026, all 374 coffee shops rented from HDB will offer budget meals.

sections.label: Budget meals at privately-owned coffee shops
sections.summary: HDB engages the 402 sold, privately-owned coffee shops to join the Budget Meal initiative and now requires new buyers to offer budget meals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As for the 402 HDB coffee shops that were sold and hence now privately-owned, we have been engaging them to join the Budget Meal initiative and are studying other measures, including Mr Murali’s suggestion to make budget meal provisions compulsory for privately-owned coffee shops who want to renew their Outdoor Refreshment Area (ORA) applications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: HDB has started requiring new buyers of privately-owned coffee shops to offer budget meals when they take over the premises.

sections.label: R360 case closure requirements
sections.summary: Under R360, more straightforward cases must be closed only when work is completed, with photo evidence where practicable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As part of our Resolution 360 (R360) initiative, we are addressing this disconnect.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We now require more categories of straightforward cases to be closed not when agencies have instructed their contractors to take action, but only when the work has actually been completed with photo evidence where practicable.

sections.label: Feedback resolution results
sections.summary: Feedback resolution speed doubled and resident satisfaction rose 20 percentage-points while using less manpower.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The speed of feedback resolution has doubled, while resident satisfaction has improved by 20 percentage-points, all while using less manpower.

sections.label: Pilot team, coffee shops, budget meals
sections.summary: The pilot team works with volunteers and agencies, awaiting legislated powers by end-2024; budget meal plans cover coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To Mr Derrick Goh's question, the initial pilot team is working closely with grassroots volunteers, HDB and other agencies to familiarise itself with case handling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It will be able to do more when we have legislated the requisite powers, alongside enhancements to the mediation framework and the CDRT process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We hope to complete this by the end of 2024 and I look forward to support from Members of this House when we do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As for the 402 sold public housing estate coffee shops, we have invited operators to join the budget meal plan and are studying other proposals, including the requirement for private coffee shops applying to renew their Outdoor Refreshment Area applications to provide budget meals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: HDB has begun to require new buyers of private coffee shops to provide budget meals upon taking over the coffee shop.

sections.label: Jurong Lake Gardens completion
sections.summary: Lakeside Garden was completed last year, and the revamped Chinese and Japanese Gardens will open this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, we completed Lakeside Garden within Jurong Lake Gardens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This year, we will open the revamped Chinese and Japanese Gardens, thereby completing Jurong Lake Gardens.

sections.label: Therapeutic gardens, Nature Ways, park connectors
sections.summary: There are 14 therapeutic gardens, around 210 kilometres of Nature Ways and over 380 kilometres of park connectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These gardens are more natural in design, bringing about greater sensory experiences that improve the well-being of visitors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We now have a total of 14 therapeutic gardens and are on track to achieve our goal of 30 such gardens by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To date, we have established around 210 kilometres of Nature Ways and over 380 kilometres of park connectors, including the first phase of the Round Island Route.

sections.label: Singapore skyrise greenery added
sections.summary: Singapore added almost 40 hectares of skyrise greenery last year, reaching 190 hectares islandwide.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year alone, Singapore added almost 40 hectares of skyrise greenery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This brings us to 190 hectares across the island – the equivalent of over 270 football fields.

sections.label: Measures to manage animals
sections.summary: Measures include habitat modification, translocation of animals away from urban areas, and direct population control to protect public safety and reduce disamenities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The range of measures includes habitat modification to reduce food sources, the translocation of animals away from urban areas and direct population control where necessary to protect public safety and/or reduce disamenities.

sections.label: Action against bird feeding
sections.summary: In each of the past three years, NParks took action against more than 170 bird feeding cases, ranging from warnings to prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In each of the past three years, NParks has taken action against more than 170 cases of bird feeding, with actions ranging from warnings to prosecution, depending on the severity of the case.

sections.label: Disease outbreak research programme
sections.summary: Training and capacity building efforts are integrated, and research will be stepped up through a new $15-million Biosurveillance Research Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are also integrating our training and capacity building efforts and work closely together to investigate and manage disease outbreaks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will be stepping up research through a new $15-million Biosurveillance Research Programme.

sections.label: Veterinary Council establishment
sections.summary: A Veterinary Council will be established to regulate professional standards and practices in the local vet sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: As announced last October, we will be establishing a Veterinary Council to regulate professional standards and practices in the local vet sector.

sections.label: Licensing and microchipping pet cats
sections.summary: A key proposal was to license and microchip pet cats and allow up to two cats per HDB household.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: A key proposal was to license and microchip pet cats and to allow up to two cats per HDB household.

sections.label: Therapeutic gardens and park connectors
sections.summary: Last year five therapeutic gardens were launched, bringing the total to 14, and over 380 kilometres of park connectors were established.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched five therapeutic gardens, bringing the total to 14.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We have also established over 380 kilometres of park connectors.

sections.label: Biosurveillance Research Programme funding
sections.summary: A new $15 million Biosurveillance Research Programme will step up research in this field.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Through a new $15 million Biosurveillance Research Programme, we will step up research in this field.

sections.label: ComLink Rental Scheme families
sections.summary: Since November 2022, all families with children enter public rental housing through the ComLink Rental Scheme, with around 700 families as of end January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since November 2022, all families with children enter public rental housing through the ComLink Rental Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As of end January 2024, we have around 700 families on this scheme.

sections.label: Public rental households home ownership
sections.summary: About 8,300 public rental households progressed to home ownership over the past decade, with close to 950 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, about 8,300 public rental households have progressed to home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: In 2023 alone, close to 950 households transitioned to home ownership, the highest in the last five years.

sections.label: SRSF pilot applications
sections.summary: HDB will open applications for the SRSF pilot in the second quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: HDB will open applications for the SRSF pilot in the second quarter 2024.

sections.label: Wireless AAS expansion rollout
sections.summary: About 800 seniors received emergency medical assistance via wireless AAS from end-2019 to mid-2023, and expansion from January 2025 will cover three rental blocks monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Like Mr Abdul Rahim, about 800 seniors have received emergency medical assistance through the wireless AAS from end-2019 to mid-2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The wireless AAS expansion is estimated to benefit around 26,800 more seniors living in around 170 rental blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that we will start to roll out the wireless AAS expansion from January 2025 and will cover three rental blocks per month.

sections.label: Enhanced SDS downpayment reduction
sections.summary: From June 2024, the SDS will be enhanced to reduce the initial downpayment to 2.5% of the flat price, with the balance paid at key collection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: From June 2024, we will enhance the SDS to further reduce the initial downpayment to 2.5% of the flat price, with the balance to be paid when they collect their keys.

sections.label: PPHS supply and vouchers
sections.summary: PPHS supply will double to 4,000 units by 2025, with vouchers in place for one year from July 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: To meet the high demand for PPHS, we will double the supply of PPHS to 4,000 units by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The vouchers will be in place for one year, from July 2024.

sections.label: AAS provision expansion
sections.summary: The expansion of AAS provision is expected to benefit around 26,800 seniors living in 170 rental blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The expansion of AAS provision is expected to benefit around 26,800 seniors living in 170 rental blocks.

sections.label: Staggered Downpayment Scheme enhancement
sections.summary: The enhancement to the Staggered Downpayment Scheme is one mechanism helping young couples ready to settle down get their flat faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Indeed the enhancement to the Staggered Downpayment Scheme is one mechanism by which we help young couples who are ready and prepared to settle down and set up family to get their flat faster.

sections.label: Bringing down waiting times
sections.summary: Waiting times were brought under control and construction time reduced through catch up, working with contractors and suppliers, and Shorter Waiting Time flats launched in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The second, of course, is to bring down waiting times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There were disruptions across the board but we have brought it under control and brought down overall construction time, firstly by catch up, and secondly by working with our contractors, with our suppliers in order to build more effectively and build more quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also, as I mentioned earlier, started in 2018 to launch Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sections.label: New housing supply mix
sections.summary: New housing supply combines BTO flats, Shorter Waiting Time flats, Sale of Balance Flats, open selection flats and the resale market with grants, plus the First-Timer scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And the overall mix of new housing supply will be a combination of BTO flats, Shorter Waiting Time flats, Sale of Balance Flats and open selection flats, and, of course, the resale market with grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also help young couples through the First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) scheme to support them amidst all the first-timers who are applying and this would be young couples who have gotten married and are trying to buy their very first home.

sections.label: Mountbatten Parking Heroes signage
sections.summary: Funding helped volunteers design and install signages to deter illegal parking in Mountbatten, with feedback volume at intervention sites falling by some 26% from 2021 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: They call themselves The Mountbatten Parking Heroes and what our funding did was to assist this group of volunteers in designing and installing creative signages to deter illegal parking in specific spots in Mountbatten.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This has gotten quite good results, because from 2021 to 2022, the feedback volume on illegal parking at specific intervention sites fell by some 26%.

sections.label: Noise experiential lab HDB
sections.summary: A noise experiential lab in an HDB setting let visitors explore inter-floor noise travel and role-play interventions like mats, furniture and socks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: One was through the noise experiential lab that we set up last year and ran for a few months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It was set up in an HDB setting which allows visitors to explore how noise that is created through everyday activities can travel inter-floor and also to role-play the different interventions that residents could do, for instance by interacting with neighbours, asking them to keep their noise down, testing out the effects of, for instance, using mats or furniture, socks, and seeing the reduction in the noise experience by someone in another neighbouring unit.

sections.label: Working with AfAs
sections.summary: Public and community education is supported by working with AfAs, with positive experience on the AfAction on joss paper burning norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Another way in which we support public education and community education is through working with AfAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have had a very positive experience on the AfAction on joss paper burning norms.

sections.label: Shorter waiting time flats
sections.summary: About 2,800 shorter waiting time flats are being offered this year, one year ahead of the commitment to ramp up from next year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Shorter waiting time flats, 2,800 or thereabouts this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: So, one year ahead of our commitment, which was to start ramping up shorter waiting time from next year.

sections.label: Limits on shorter waiting flats
sections.summary: Meeting existing demand and catching up on COVID-19 delayed flats limits shorter waiting time flats, and BTO launches need 10 to 15 years lead time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Why can we not have 50% shorter waiting time flats this year?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We have still to meet existing demand in addition to doing the catch-up for all the delayed flats as a result of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: I think that really is the rate-limiting factor and, as we have explained previously in this House and to the media, when you want to launch a BTO project, it can take up to 10 to 15 years of lead time, of land preparation, of allowing the prior user to complete the use of the land; and for the land to be taken back, and so on and so forth.

sections.label: Long-term public housing planning
sections.summary: Land uses run out and launches take 10 to 15 years, so planning must model household formation amid smaller families, singles and reconstituted families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: The uses of the land will run out, whether it is for recreation, business, industry, horse racing so on and so forth, all these we will have to plan for it in the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: And as we say, you want to prepare for a launch, take 10 to 15 years, you also have to model as best as you can what your projected household formation is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: And we are already starting to see for a number of years now smaller families, more singles living alone, more reconstituted families and so on, and we want to be able to make sure we meet not just the needs of the singles but the needs of many other groups as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: So, all in, I make a call to Members from both sides of the House to recognise that, in Singapore, we are able to achieve public housing for the masses despite these tremendous limitations and it requires long-term planning, discipline, give-and-take and also a sense that we all have our needs, but we all also need to think of other groups of Singaporeans, especially the vulnerable ones.

sections.label: Intensification for housing needs
sections.summary: Intensification is a strategy to fit Singaporeans' needs and aspirations into the one island city-state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Intensification is one of the strategies that allows us to fit all the needs and some of the aspirations of Singaporeans today and tomorrow into this one and only island city-state.

sections.label: Mixed use land strategy
sections.summary: The mixed-use strategy stacks land uses vertically, with examples including Bishan, Tampines Hub and Heartbeat@Bedok.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The second strategy, of course, is mixed use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And the Member talked about the potential for more projects, like he mentioned Bishan, there is also Tampines Hub, there is also Heartbeat@Bedok, and many others, where land uses are stacked vertically instead of horizontally by giving each one parcel of land.

sections.label: Brownfield site redevelopment plans
sections.summary: The passage asks why brownfield sites like Gillman Barracks are planned for redevelopment while Kranji Turf Club and Bukit Timah Turf City are taken back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of brownfield sites, why are we planning for the redevelopment or the use of a brownfield site like Gillman Barracks when we are taking back Kranji Turf Club, as well as starting to develop Bukit Timah Turf City?

sections.label: Carving recreation from limited space
sections.summary: URA and partner agencies devise ways to carve recreation from limited space, such as bringing activities into one space at Bukit Canberra and Heartbeat@Bedok.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: URA and its partner agencies have been working very hard to devise different ways to carve out recreation out of this limited space and there are different ways in which they do it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, one example will be to bring different activities into the same space, such as at Bukit Canberra and Heartbeat@Bedok.

sections.label: EASE programme household beneficiaries
sections.summary: As of 31 January 2024, more than 309,300 households benefited from the EASE programme, through the Home Improvement Programme and direct application.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As of 31 January 2024, I am happy to share that more than 309,300 households have benefited from the EASE programme and they did it in conjunction with the Home Improvement Programme, as well as direct application.

sections.label: HFE and flat downpayment process
sections.summary: A working couple applying for HFE learns their EHG and HDB loan amounts, then books a flat and pays 5% to 10% downpayment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Currently, if a young couple has been working, say, for more than a year, when they apply for HFE, they will have a sense of (a) how much EHG they will get; and (b) how much HDB loan they can get.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Then, with that, they book a flat and pay between 5% and 10% of the downpayment, that is, 5% if they take the Staggered Downpayment Scheme HDB loan; 10% if you take a financial institution (FI) loan.

sections.label: Town Councils lift replacement funding
sections.summary: Under the Town Councils Act section 47(5), Town Councils may use LRF for lift replacement capital expenditure, including items replaced under 10 years and LUP works.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Under the Town Council's Act, section 47(5), Town Councils are already allowed to use LRF for any capital expenditure related to the replacement of lifts in residential or commercial property, including items that are replaced at less than 10 years' intervals and lift upgrading works under HDB's LUP in residential property or commercial property.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Examples of uses would include the replacement of lift position display panels, replacement of lift inverters, replacement of hoisting ropes and the sheaves of lifts and so forth.

sections.label: HDB coffee shop rents
sections.summary: HDB may reduce rent at renewal for poorly performing coffee shops and re-tender returned ones on PQM, so rents can fall.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Sim, short reply as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: There may be some HDB-owned coffee shops that do not do well, perhaps due to low footfall.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In such cases, where the stalls are concerned, generally, we leave it to the operators to decide how to attract new tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But if the entire coffee shop is not doing well, then, at the point of rent renewal, HDB is prepared to reduce rent if it is warranted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: And if the operator returns the coffee shop to HDB, then, we will re-tender on the basis of PQM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Because we do not have a guide rent, therefore, if all the bids that we receive are lower than the rents we have gotten in the past, then, it is possible for the rents to go even lower.
